title: Indian Software Stocks Set to Beat AI Peers by Most in Decades
source_used: Bloomberg (text read via Business Standard, which carries the Bloomberg report)
key_facts: An index of India's biggest software exporters rose over 10% this week while an MSCI gauge of global chip stocks fell 7.4%.
That puts the former on course for its biggest weekly outperformance since 2004.
AI shares fell on slowing revenue growth, infrastructure-financing worries and renewed rate-hike fears.
Societe Generale's Rajat Agarwal said foreign investors may look at Indian IT stocks if the chip correction continues.
The Nifty IT Index has climbed more than 22% from its July low but is still down about 17% this year; it trades under 17 times forward earnings.
Morgan Stanley analysts said the sector lacks near-term catalysts; Infosys reports second-quarter results on 23 Oct, with revenue growth of 1.8% expected.
HCL Technologies raised its full-year sales growth guidance this week.
quote_evidence: India's information-technology stocks are poised to beat their global semiconductor rivals by the most in two decades this week, with analysts saying the sector is set to keep outperforming as the artificial-intelligence rally unwinds.
"Although valuations appear reasonable now, on a relative and absolute basis, the sector lacks near-term catalysts," Morgan Stanley analysts led by Gaurav Rateria wrote in a note this week.
why_it_matters_hint: Money is rotating from AI chip stocks toward cheaper Indian software exporters.
